Arjun: Quick sync requestwe need a compact canonical for TTFT vs TPOT, goodput vs QPS, and a minimal harness config for applespec comparability.
Zoe: +1. Our last bench PR had inconsistent definitions, made cross-kernel comparisons noisy.
Matt: Can we make the measurement windows explicitwarmup/stabilize/steady-state? Thats been the biggest source of variance.
BenchBot: job/bench-1712344412 started by Arjun  harness=replay trace=prod-2025-11 sample=5% kernels=[auto,mm,q8]
Arjun: My proposed canonical definitions (short):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): time from request arrival at runtime to the first byte emitted. Include server-side serialization/transmission. Report p50/p95/p99.
- TPOT (time-to-last-token): time from request arrival to final token emitted. Use for multi-token streams. Report p50/p95 and include mean token-rate.
- QPS: raw accepted requests/sec at ingress (counts all accepted requests regardless of outcome).
- Goodput: fraction of requests that (a) finish within configured SLO latency and (b) did not fall back to a lower-accuracy kernel. Report as percentage and as effective RPS (good requests/sec).
Zoe: When publishing goodput, always include kernel-map and fallback counts so consumers can see cost/quality tradeoffs.
Matt: KV-cache rules: a noisy source of p95 changes. Recommend: prefill or warmup-by-count/seconds. I suggest kv_warmup_count=2000 OR kv_warmup_secs=60 (use whichever completes first).
Sara: Agreed. Canonical windows we should enforce:
- Warmup: first 60s OR first 2k requests (whichever first) — do not include these in peak claims.
- Stabilization: next 120s — collect metrics but mark as transient.
- Steady-state: next 10 minutes — compute final p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
Zoe: For short runs (<5m) mandate synthetic KV prefill (script included) so steady-state metrics are valid.
Arjun: Recommended bench command for applespec runs (example):
```
bench run \n  --harness=replay \n  --trace=prod/2025-11-03 \n  --kernels=mm,q8,auto \n  --batch-policy='latency_target_ms:50' \n  --kv-warmup-count=2000 \n  --sample=0.05 \n  --run-seconds=900
```
Sara: Telemetry fields to capture (required): emit_kernel, emit_kv_hit, emit_batch_shape, emit_fallback_event, emit_trace_id. Provide a short telemetry snippet in the harness config.
Zoe: Latency reporting rules: show p50/p95/p99 for both TTFT and TPOT. Also include p99/p95 ratio (tail-index) and 99th percentile of fallback-switch latency (time from decision to kernel-emission).
Matt: Regression triage checklist (if p95 increases >10%):
1) KV hitrate over steady-state window
2) fallback fraction and which kernels were used
3) batch-shape distribution (spikes in max batch size)
4) GPU saturation/context-switch counters
5) kernel-selection logs for slow paths
Arjun: Applespec invariants (mandatory for apples-to-apples):
- identical trace and sample seed
- explicit kernel set (avoid auto) for final comparison
- same batch-policy and scheduling config
- same KV prefill method (prefill script or replay warmup)
- identical telemetry enabled
Zoe: Publishing checklist for bench owners: include a 1-paragraph summary (what changed, SLO impact, quality tradeoffs), link to artifact(s), and a small table: kernel -> fallback_count -> goodput_RPS -> p95_TTFT.
Matt: Ill add a prefill helper script to the harness repo and a README using these invariants.
Sara: Ill clone a Grafana dashboard for kernel/fallback/kv_hit/batch_shape so reviewers can eyeball anomalies quickly.
